metadata.title: Message 30 Costs 31 Times More
metadata.purpose: Teach viewers how token accumulation works in Claude sessions and which 23 habits cut waste — without hitting usage limits.

props.command: What is: Message 30 Costs 31 Times More?

beats.narration_text: Annyeong. This is Liam, in for Bear. [Claude Composer: 'Why do I keep hitting my usage limit by 2pm?'] [Answer lands: 'Because message 30 re-reads 29 full exchanges before answering you.']

props.ask: Why do I keep hitting my usage limit by 2pm?
props.answer_preview: Because message 30 re-reads 29 full exchanges before it even starts on your question.
props.command: Why do I keep hitting my usage limit by 2pm?

beats.narration_text: Claude counts tokens — roughly one per word. And here is the brutal part: every single message, Claude re-reads your entire conversation from the very top. Message one costs almost nothing. Message thirty? Claude just re-read twenty-nine exchanges before thinking about your new question.

illustration.concept: Animated token-cost growth curve: horizontal axis = message number 1–30, vertical axis = tokens consumed. A glowing dot traces the exponential rise. At message 30 a bold callout reads '31× message 1'.
illustration.layout: full-bleed chart, warm ink on cream, single terracotta annotation line at message 30

beats.narration_text: First habit cluster: fix your files before you upload. A single PDF page burns fifteen-hundred to three-thousand tokens. A full screenshot costs thirteen-hundred. Extract the text, paste into markdown, upload clean prose instead.

card.sub: PDF page = 1,500–3,000 tokens. Clean text = a fraction. Export to .md before uploading.

beats.narration_text: Second cluster: plan in Chat, build in Cowork. Chat is lightweight. Cowork is heavy. Work out your structure and assumptions in Chat first — then drop into Cowork with a precise brief. Also: batch your tasks. Three prompts equals three full context reloads. One prompt with three tasks equals one.

illustration.concept: Split-lane diagram. Left lane labelled CHAT: sticky-note sketch of structure. Right lane labelled COWORK: final file being built. An arrow bridges them with the word 'then'. Below: a second row shows 3 separate message bubbles (costly) vs 1 combined bubble (efficient).
illustration.layout: two-column comparison on cream, lane headers in terracotta, arrow in warm ink

beats.narration_text: Third cluster: let Claude pull context from you. A five-hundred-word prompt costs five-hundred tokens every re-read. A thirty-word prompt that triggers AskUserQuestion — and you click options — costs almost nothing per turn. Short prompt, click answers, fewer reloads.

card.sub: 'I want [task]. Ask me questions with AskUserQuestion before you start.' Clicks cost almost nothing.

beats.narration_text: Fourth cluster: surgical redos and the edit button. When section three is wrong, say 'only redo section three, keep everything else.' A full redo re-generates every token. In Chat you can also click Edit on your original message — the old exchange gets replaced, not stacked. Edit instead of correcting saves you from piling onto a history Claude re-reads forever.

card.sub: Click Edit on your Chat prompt. Surgical: 'only redo section 3.' Every follow-up stacks history.

beats.narration_text: Fifth cluster: match the tool to the task and cap your context. Quick question — Chat with Haiku. Deep report on your files — Cowork with Opus. Keep About Me files under two thousand words; Cowork reads the whole folder before every task. Use Projects for recurring files — upload once, it caches. And restart every fifteen to twenty messages before the session becomes a token furnace.

illustration.concept: Three-row tool-match table: row 1: 'Quick question' → Chat + Haiku icon; row 2: 'Deep report' → Cowork + Opus icon; row 3: 'Build a chart' → Code + Sonnet icon. To the right, a sidebar callout: 'About Me < 2,000 words' and 'Restart @ 15–20 msgs'.
illustration.layout: table on cream, row labels in terracotta, tool names in SF Mono, sidebar callout in warm ink box

beats.narration_text: Your turn. This week: pick three habits. If you use Cowork daily, start with habits one, two, and five — convert files, plan in Chat, surgical redos. If you mostly use Chat, start with eight, fifteen, and seventeen — edit don't correct, new chat per topic, Projects for recurring files. If you're on the twenty-dollar plan and keep hitting the wall, try six, thirteen, and twenty-two — batch prompts, cheaper models, spread sessions across the day.

card.sub: Cowork daily → habits 1, 2, 5. Chat user → 8, 15, 17. On $20 plan → 6, 13, 22.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this: your Claude sessions keep running out of context or hitting usage limits before the task is done. Ask Claude to show you the session-length economics: why the cost of a message at the end of a long session is much higher than at the start, how to structure multi-step tasks to stay within a session, and when to start a new session rather than continuing the current one.
